newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold falls on bullion, weak U.K debut.
newsitem.headline: Randgold falls on bullion, weak U.K debut.

text.p: Shares in South African mining group Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd tumbled over 14 percent to a fresh year low, buffeted by a falling bullion price and following a low listing price for its Randgold Resources' London debut.
By 1345 GMT Randgold stocks listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange were down 325 cents or 14.2 percent at 19.50 rand in moderate volume of 176,400 shares.

Analysts said that most gold shares were taking a knock from bullion's slide over the weekend to its lowest levels in 4-1/4 years, but that Randgold was more exposed than most due to the marginal nature of its mines and focus on gold activities.
"The Randgold mines are more marginal than other mines in other groups," said Nick Goodwin, an analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.

Mines in the Randgold stable include Buffelsfontein Gold Mines which was last down 74 cents at a new 1997 low of 906 cents and Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd which also slumped to a year low of 20.75 rand -- a fall of 125 cents.

"And Randgold, like Gold Fields, 100 percent of their earnings come from gold," Goodwin said, adding that mining houses Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Gencor Ltd were protected from gold price gyrations by their other activities.
Randgold shares already took a beating last week following the lower-than-expected listing price of its exploration arm Randgold Resources on the London Stock Exchange.
"The Randgold Resources listing price was not as successful as people thought it would be," Goodwin said.

The offer had been set at $16.50 per share -- lower than the $18 to $23 range expected originally by Randgold chairman Peter Flack and the size of the offer was also down at five million shares -- instead of the expected seven million.

The poorer pricing was blamed in part on gold's downturn to below $340 an ounce and the continuing impact on investors of the Bre-X scandal, where a Canadian junior exploration firm vastly overstated the potential of a gold find in Indonesia.
